stories.title: Blood marker of nerve damage only partly predicted MS progression
stories.summary: In 262 people with early MS who started interferon beta-1a, blood levels of neurofilament light chain predicted progression only until MRI results were counted. Rising levels in year two went with faster brain shrinkage later.
stories.why: It shows a blood test may help track the disease, but it is not ready to guide care on its own.

stories.title: Fatigue score and a spinal fluid protein tied to hidden MS progression
stories.summary: In a small study of 81 people with relapsing MS, a fatigue questionnaire score and a protein in spinal fluid were linked to worsening without relapses. The authors say the findings are exploratory and need to be confirmed in other groups.

stories.title: Indirect comparison suggests Briumvi may slow disability more than two rivals
stories.summary: A statistical comparison of separate trials linked Briumvi to a lower risk of disability progression than Ocrevus or Kesimpta. It was funded by a company that sells the drug, and no head-to-head trial has tested it.
stories.why: Treat it as a hint, not proof, and talk with your neurologist before drawing conclusions.

stories.title: Ear-based nerve stimulation is being tested for hand problems in MS
stories.summary: A University of Colorado trial of about 70 adults is testing mild stimulation through the ear during hand exercises. No results yet; the main goal is safety.
stories.why: Hopes come from animal and stroke research, so it is unproven in people with MS.

stories.title: Lab-grown 3D mini-brain may help test drugs that repair MS damage
stories.summary: Researchers built a rice-grain-sized model from human stem cells to study myelin damage and repair. This is lab work only, not tested in people.

stories.title: Physical activity and MS risk: a possible link only with low sun exposure
stories.summary: In a Swedish study of about 3,000 people with MS and 5,800 without, activity alone was not clearly linked to MS risk. Among people with low sun exposure, the most active had 24% lower odds, a link, not proof.

stories.title: Parental stress may help explain low self-esteem in teens with MS
stories.summary: In a small study of 30 Israeli children and teens with MS, fatigue and slower thinking were tied to lower self-esteem, partly through parental stress. It was a single snapshot, so it cannot show cause.
stories.why: Support for families may matter as much as support for the child.

stories.title: Melatonin for MS: benefits still unclear, review finds
stories.summary: A review of 10 studies with 435 people with MS found no clear proof that melatonin supplements reduce relapses, disability or new MRI activity. High doses raised liver concerns.
stories.why: It shows melatonin is not a proven MS treatment, though it is often sold for sleep.

stories.title: Generic MS pills showed more varied biomarker results than brand names
stories.summary: A look back at 1,124 people with relapsing-remitting MS found more variable blood protein markers with generic teriflunomide, fingolimod and dimethyl fumarate. The study had no data on symptoms or scans, so what it means for patients is unclear.

stories.title: 15 years of safety reports on MS drugs reviewed
stories.summary: Researchers studied about 500,000 U.S. adverse event reports for MS disease-modifying drugs and found different drugs tied to different side effect patterns, such as PML with natalizumab and infections with anti-CD20 drugs. The authors say reports like these cannot show how common a side effect is or which drug is safer.
stories.why: It is not a reason to change treatment; talk with your neurologist about any concerns.

stories.title: Stem cell transplant may calm lingering inflammation in MS, small study suggests
stories.summary: In 30 adults with MS who had a stem cell transplant, some MRI markers of long-lasting inflammation (called rim lesions) faded and no new ones appeared. The study was small, had no comparison group, and the authors say larger studies are needed.
stories.why: It hints at how doctors might one day tell who benefits most from a transplant.

stories.title: Ocrevus matched fingolimod on relapses in children with MS, with fewer new lesions
stories.summary: In a phase 3 trial of 187 children and teens with relapsing MS, Ocrevus worked about as well as fingolimod for relapses and led to fewer new brain lesions on MRI. Infusion reactions were common, mostly mild or moderate. The trial was run by the drug's maker, Roche.
stories.why: Children with MS have had few treatment studies, so more data helps families and doctors choose.

stories.title: Pain linked to feeling foggy, but not to test scores
stories.summary: In 396 adults at one Canadian MS clinic, more pain went with more self-reported thinking and memory trouble. Their actual test results did not match how they felt.
stories.why: It suggests pain, mood and fatigue may affect how thinking feels, and are worth mentioning to a care team.

stories.title: Vitamin D receptor gene variants tied to MS symptoms in Greek study
stories.summary: In 200 people with MS and 265 without, no single gene variant differed by MS status. Some variants were linked to motor symptoms and neck spinal cord lesions, a link, not proof.

stories.title: Christina Applegate says doctors now doubt her MS diagnosis
stories.summary: The actor said on her podcast that a doctor told her she does not have MS and that the cause of her symptoms is unknown. Neurologists say MS can be misdiagnosed because no single test confirms it.
stories.why: It is a reminder that MS diagnosis relies on criteria, and a specialist can review a diagnosis that does not fit.

stories.title: Early CAR-T results in 3 people with progressive MS
stories.summary: At a major MS meeting, researchers reported a donor-cell CAR-T therapy called CTA313 in just three people with progressive MS. After 3 months, two improved slightly and one stayed stable; side effects were mild.
stories.why: Very small and early, so it shows only that this idea is being tested safely.

stories.title: Podcast: why dizziness and vertigo happen in MS
stories.summary: A physiotherapist explains how the body's balance system works, why MS can cause dizziness, vertigo and balance trouble, and what treatment and support exist.

stories.title: Experimental pill fenebrutinib lowered markers of chronic brain inflammation
stories.summary: Company-reported trial data say fenebrutinib cut slowly expanding lesions by up to 30% and relapses by 55% versus Aubagio in relapsing MS. The trials are still ongoing and the drug is not yet approved.
stories.why: If approved, it could add a new oral option; the FDA decision is expected in early 2027.

stories.title: One death reported in CAR-T trial for MS as early results look promising
stories.summary: Bristol Myers Squibb reported one patient died of septic pneumonia 44 days after a CAR-T infusion. Early data in 66 people (safety was the main goal) also showed promising signs in some with progressive MS.
stories.why: CAR-T for MS is still experimental and carries real risks, such as serious immune reactions.

stories.title: Progressive MS pill vidofludimus: disability trends held in open-label extension
stories.summary: In an extension of a phase 2 trial, disability trends from the main trial were kept up by people who stayed on the drug, with no new safety concerns. There was no placebo group, and the main trial missed its brain-volume goal.

stories.title: About 4 in 10 adults with MS in a Thai study were at risk of poor nutrition
stories.summary: A small single-center study in Thailand found about 42% of 100 adults with MS were malnourished or at risk. Poorer nutrition went with lower body weight and more disability, but this design cannot show cause.
stories.why: Eating well is part of care, and it is fine to ask your care team about it.

stories.title: Early CAR-T results in 26 people with progressive MS
stories.summary: Company news: in a small early-stage study, most people tracked kept stable or better disability scores, and no new MRI lesions were seen. Follow-up was short and there was no comparison group.

stories.title: Ocrevus worked similarly in people over 55, company reports
stories.summary: Company news: in a trial, 53% of people over 55 had no disability progression after two years, close to 55% in younger people. Results come from a conference presentation.
stories.why: Older adults are often left out of MS trials, so this is useful to see.

stories.title: Poorer vision-related quality of life went with more depression symptoms
stories.summary: In a study of 458 adults in China with MS or a related condition (NMOSD), those who felt vision problems hurt daily life were more likely to screen positive for depression. This was a snapshot in time, so it cannot show cause.
stories.why: It suggests that how vision problems affect daily life, not only how bad the vision is, may be worth mentioning to a care team.

stories.title: Company reports CAR-T cell therapy held disability steady in a few people with progressive MS
stories.summary: Kyverna reported that 5 of 6 people with progressive MS in a small early trial at Stanford were stable or improved, with no severe cytokine reactions. This is company news from a very small, uncontrolled study.

stories.title: Switching to injected Ocrevus was well tolerated in a real-world study
stories.summary: In 296 people who switched from IV Ocrevus to the under-the-skin version, no new safety problems appeared and injection-site reactions were rare and mild. Most switched by patient preference.
stories.why: This may matter to people who would rather avoid long infusion visits.

stories.title: Blurry vision in MS is not always an optic neuritis relapse
stories.summary: At a major eye meeting, doctors discussed a records study finding that people with MS-type disease and past optic neuritis had about twice the 5-year risk of uveitis (eye inflammation), though the absolute risk was low at 1.1% versus 0.6%.

stories.title: Fenebrutinib pill cut relapses 55% versus teriflunomide in relapsing MS
stories.summary: Company news: Roche says two combined phase 3 trials found the experimental pill cut yearly relapses by 55% over 96 weeks compared with teriflunomide, and slowed brain shrinkage. Disability worsening was 16% lower.
stories.why: It shows how far this pill has come, but it is not yet approved.

stories.title: Yale team links Epstein-Barr virus activity genes to MS risk
stories.summary: In a conference presentation of work not yet peer reviewed, researchers studied over 600,000 people and found gene regions tied to Epstein-Barr virus activity that overlap with MS risk genes. A small look at 38 people found infected immune cells carrying MS-risk activity.
stories.why: It adds to the evidence on how the common virus may contribute to MS.

stories.title: CAR-T therapy zola-cel: early results in 66 people with relapsing or progressive MS
stories.summary: Company news: in a small early-stage trial with no comparison group, most people checked after 6 months had stable or improved disability. Serious side effects occurred, and one person died of pneumonia after treatment.
stories.why: It is early safety data, not proof the treatment works or is ready for patients.

stories.title: A tailored talk-therapy program eased depression in newly diagnosed MS
stories.summary: In a small randomized study of 60 adults in Australia, 63% who had 8 weeks of tailored cognitive behavioral therapy had a clear drop in depression, versus 33% with supportive listening. The benefit was still seen at week 28.
stories.why: Low mood is common early in MS, and this suggests talk therapy built for MS may help.

stories.title: MS shaped family planning for nearly half of women in an Australian survey
stories.summary: Among 270 people with MS aged 18 to 50, MS affected family planning for nearly half of women and almost a third of men. Many said they never got information on fertility or contraception, and about half wanted the talk to start at diagnosis.

stories.title: Free online talk today: staying active for brain health
stories.summary: The European MS Platform is hosting an online webinar, Movement for Brain Health, on Thursday, October 29 from 16:00 to 17:00 Central European Time. A sports neuroscientist from TU Dortmund University and a patient advocate will speak; sign-up is on the event page.
stories.why: It covers staying active at different ability levels.

stories.title: People with MS forgot more after one week in a small German study
stories.summary: In a study of 62 people with MS and 65 without, both groups remembered similarly at 30 minutes. A week later, the MS group remembered less.
stories.why: Memory tests that wait a week may catch problems that quick tests miss.

stories.title: Willingness to get vaccines fell among German adults with MS
stories.summary: In 175 adults followed for five years, willingness to get all recommended vaccines fell from 81% to 66%. Doctors discussing vaccines rose from 34% to 71%.

stories.title: Updated MS diagnosis rules found MS earlier in a six-center European study
stories.summary: The 2024 criteria led to diagnosis in about 4 months on average, versus about 16 with the 2017 rules, and caught more people (82% vs 63%). The study had no control group and short follow-up.
stories.why: Earlier diagnosis can mean earlier treatment.

stories.title: Early MS drugs differed on relapses but not disability over 2 years
stories.summary: In 509 newly diagnosed adults in Europe, B-cell-depleting drugs were tied to fewer relapses and slightly smaller lesion growth than pills. Disability did not differ between treatments.
stories.why: This was an observational study, so it shows a link, not proof, and only two years were tracked.

stories.title: Health-professional-led exercise programs for MS look workable, review finds
stories.summary: A review of 25 studies covering 28 programs found they seemed acceptable and doable for adults with MS. None had been tested in routine clinical care yet.

stories.title: More physical disability went with poorer thinking skills in MS
stories.summary: A review of 223 studies found greater physical disability was linked to lower scores on thinking tests, mostly in advanced disease. Thinking problems also showed up with mild physical disability.
stories.why: Thinking changes can be missed by standard disability checks.

stories.title: Rituximab tied to a higher chance of bowel disease in a large Swedish study
stories.summary: In nearly 14,000 treatment episodes, bowel disease (mostly Crohn's) was more common with rituximab than with three other MS drugs. It was still rare: under 2% of people in any group within 10 years. This is a link, not proof.
stories.why: If you take rituximab, this is something to ask your neurologist about; the study says the risk should be weighed against its benefits.

stories.title: Experts: MS activity, day-to-day impact and progression are separate things
stories.summary: In a panel discussion, MS specialists said inflammation, everyday symptoms and slow worsening of disability can each happen without the others. They say treatments now control relapses well, so future work should focus on progression. This is expert opinion, not a new study.

stories.title: Blood tests for MS activity are moving toward routine use, company expert says
stories.summary: In an interview, a maker of an MS blood test said such tests may catch silent disease activity and help with treatment choices. Insurance coverage and access to blood draws remain hurdles. This is company news, and its ability to predict future disease is not yet shown.

stories.title: Nasal spray foralumab: mixed results in a small progressive MS trial
stories.summary: Company news: a small phase 2 trial in non-active secondary progressive MS found the lower dose reduced a brain-inflammation marker on PET scans versus placebo, but the higher dose did not. The company has not released the full data.
stories.why: It is early and small, and no change in disability was seen, so it is not yet a proven treatment.

stories.title: Jack Osbourne says he sometimes feels like a "fraud" at MS events
stories.summary: On a podcast, he said he has met newer patients facing harder struggles than his. He added that MS has slowed him down at times but has not stopped him.
stories.why: Many people with MS feel they do not belong, or are not "sick enough", and he says so openly.

stories.title: Free online MS Q&A with experts, Thursday evening
stories.summary: Ohio State Wexner Medical Center is holding a free virtual question-and-answer session on Thursday, November 5, from 6:00 to 7:30 p.m. Topics include aging with MS, symptoms, diet, exercise, medicines and research.

stories.title: National MS Society opens funding for early-detection screening tools
stories.summary: The Society is asking researchers to apply for money to build and test MS screening tools that are practical to use. This is a funding call from the Society, not a study result.
stories.source: Targeted News Service (National MS Society release)

stories.title: Review finds little proof that a gluten-free diet helps MS
stories.summary: A review of six small studies found possible gains in fatigue and quality of life, but no convincing effect on MS activity or disability. The evidence was rated very low certainty, and many studies were not randomized.
stories.why: It is unclear whether any benefit came from avoiding gluten or from other diet changes made at the same time.

stories.title: Canada approves Ocrevus for children with relapsing MS
stories.summary: Health Canada approved Ocrevus, an infusion given twice a year, for relapsing-remitting MS in patients 10 and older. In a trial of 187 children and teens, it controlled relapses at least as well as fingolimod, with fewer new lesions.

stories.title: MS Education Summit in Aurora, Colorado, Saturday
stories.summary: The Rocky Mountain MS Center is hosting a morning of talks on MS care and treatment, from 9 AM to 12:15 PM. The listing says in person; the title mentions an online option, but no access details are given.

stories.title: Remibrutinib pill cut relapses versus Aubagio in two large trials
stories.summary: Company news: Novartis reports two Phase 3 trials in about 2,000 people with relapsing MS. The pill remibrutinib cut yearly relapses by 31% to 35% compared with Aubagio. Its effect on disability was not firmly proven.
stories.why: It is not approved yet; the company plans to seek approval.

stories.title: Active people with MS reported better quality of life
stories.summary: In a survey of 1,083 adults with MS, high physical activity went with better mobility, less fatigue and less walking disability. It is a link, not proof, and the data were self-reported.

stories.title: First dose given in trial of myelin-repair pill PRO-1562
stories.summary: Company news: Progentos has started an early safety trial in healthy adults in Australia. Benefits so far come only from animal studies. A later phase will test people with relapsing MS.
stories.why: No approved drug can rebuild lost myelin yet, so early trials like this are watched closely.

stories.title: Word-finding trouble in MS may be more than slow thinking
stories.summary: In a small study of 38 people with relapsing MS and 23 without, people with MS were slower and made slightly more errors on naming tasks. The errors were not fully explained by slower thinking speed.

stories.title: A 10-day ocean sailing trip looked safe in a small MS study
stories.summary: In a small study of 15 adults with mild to moderate MS and no comparison group, strength, walking, balance and thinking did not change after a 10-day sailing expedition. Most had mild or moderate seasickness, and there were no serious problems.
stories.why: It suggests sailing may be a workable way to stay active, but larger studies are needed.

stories.title: UK study puts a number on the healthcare cost of MS
stories.summary: Researchers at Bangor University looked at nearly 6,000 people with MS. Average healthcare costs were about £2,800 over three months, and almost £9,400 for people with significant disability and fast-changing disease.
stories.why: The study also found MS ranked in the lowest 10% of quality-of-life scores among common long-term conditions.

stories.title: Antioxidant add-on NAC linked to better outcomes in an early MS study
stories.summary: Jefferson University researchers added N-acetylcysteine (NAC), an antioxidant supplement, to people's usual MS treatment and report better outcomes in most. Brain scans also showed better connection between brain regions. The team says larger studies are needed.

stories.title: Workplace exposure to petroleum-based lubricants linked to higher MS odds
stories.summary: A Swedish study of about 2,900 people with MS and 6,100 without found those who reported job exposure to oils and lubricants had 38% higher odds of MS. It is a link, not proof, and exposure was self-reported.
stories.why: It adds to research on workplace and environmental factors, but it does not show that lubricants cause MS.

stories.title: Low-fat diet and fatigue in MS: small trial analysis
stories.summary: In a small four-month trial of 27 adults, fatigue scores improved in both the low-fat diet and usual-diet groups, and the difference between them could be chance. Changes in fat-related blood markers tracked with less fatigue.
stories.why: Diet is not a proven fatigue treatment yet; larger studies are needed.

stories.title: Why some people with MS turn down thinking tests
stories.summary: In one Canadian clinic, about 15% of 334 adults with MS declined free cognitive testing. Those with progressive MS or anxiety-related conditions were more likely to decline, as were those who did not report memory worries.
stories.why: Skipped testing can leave thinking changes unnoticed.

stories.title: Dutch regulator probes Biogen over Tysabri safety test access
stories.summary: The Netherlands' competition authority is examining whether Biogen unfairly kept a Tysabri safety-screening test from patients taking rival drugs, such as a biosimilar. This is an investigation, not a finding.
